overview: This chapter details the architecture and operational mechanics of an AI tutor system, beginning with its limitations regarding factual accuracy despite linguistic fluency. It covers the training pipeline involving parameter adjustment via distinct datasets (training, validation, test) to prevent data leakage, alongside internal transformer mechanics like tokenization, causal attention masks, and positional encoding. The text explains optimization processes including loss functions, backpropagation, and regularization techniques such as dropout and early stopping. Post-training strategies are addressed through weight quantization for memory efficiency and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for context augmentation. Finally, the chapter establishes a dual-evaluation framework separating retrieval metrics (recall/precision) from answer generation quality, emphasizing protocols for handling conflicting information and uncertainty.
topics: AI tutor system limitations: fluency vs. factual accuracy
Dataset management: training, validation, and test separation to prevent leakage
Transformer architecture: tokenization, embeddings, positional info, causal attention masks
Training mechanics: loss functions, backpropagation, optimizers, learning rates
Regularization strategies: dropout, early stopping, overfitting prevention
Post-training optimization: weight quantization and memory reduction
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): embeddings, similarity search, context augmentation
Evaluation framework: distinguishing retrieval quality from answer generation quality
Handling uncertainty and conflicting course passages
